introduce:
Stand with your thighs closed, and raise your hands over your head. 

Then bend your knees and come to a sitting position. 

Lean your torso forward slightly to keep your balance. Take deep breaths. Hold this position.
name: CHAIR

tips.text: Please don’t let your knees go over your toes.
Please put your weight on your heels.
This exercise is beneficial to your arms, legs and cardiovascular system.
Breathe regularly.

introduce: Stand on the floor with feet shoulder width apart, then rotate your body gently and slowly. This stretches your back and hips.\n\nRelax your shoulders. Your toes should always face forward.
name: TORSO TWIST

tips.text: Please rotate your body gently and slowly.
Your toes should always face forward.
Make sure your abs muscles are engaged.
Please relax your shoulders.
Please don\'t twist your legs.
This exercise stretches your back and hips.

introduce: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart. Raise your arms and clap over your head.
name: CLAPS OVER HEAD

tips.text: Keep your arms straight during the exercise.
Exhale as you raise your arms, and inhale as you lower them.
This exercise can warm up your shoulders.
This exercise targets your deltoids.

introduce: Lie on your back with your legs straight and your arms stretched at your sides. \n\nExhale, lift your knees and twist your legs to the left. Breathe naturally. Hold this position.
name: LYING TWIST STRETCH LEFT

tips.text: You need to do this exercise on a mat.
Please make sure your knees are together.
Please always keep your shoulders on the floor.
Breathe regularly.
You should feel a gentle stretch on your opposite waist.
You shouldn’t feel any pain.
This exercise stretches your obliques and lower back.

introduce: Lie on your back with your legs straight and your arms stretched at your sides. \n\nExhale, lift your knees and twist your legs to the right. Breathe naturally. Hold this position.
name: LYING TWIST STRETCH RIGHT

tips.text: You need to do this exercise on a mat.
Please make sure your knees are together.
Please always keep your shoulders on the floor.
Breathe regularly.
You should feel a gentle stretch on your opposite waist.
You shouldn’t feel any pain.
This exercise stretches your obliques and lower back.

introduce: Sit on the floor with your feet together, and grab your toes.\n\nOpen your knees to the sides, and press your knees down as much as possible.
name: SEATED BUTTERFLY STRETCH

tips.text: Press your knees down as much as possible.
Please keep your back straight.
Breathe regularly.

introduce: Start on all fours with your knees under your butt and your hands directly under your shoulders. \n\nStraighten your legs, and lift your hips up in an upside down \'V\' shape. Spread your feet apart, and spread your fingers. Transfer your weight back to your legs. Hold this position.
name: DOWNWARD FACING DOG

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
If it\'s too hard for you, please bend your knees slightly.
Please keep your back straight.
Please sink your shoulders.
Please keep your arms tight.
Breathe regularly.

introduce:
Stand with your feet a little wider than shoulder-width apart. Raise your arms at your sides to shoulder height with your palms down.

Turn your left foot to the left and your right foot 45 degrees to the left. Slightly shift your hips to the right, and bend your torso to the left until your left hand is pressed on the floor. 

Extend your right arm toward the ceiling, and turn your head to look at your right hand. Breathe slowly and deeply. Hold this position.
name: TRIANGLE POSE LEFT

tips.text: Please keep your chest facing forward.
Please keep your arms and legs straight during the exercise.
If you feel it\'s too hard, put your left hand on your left leg instead of the floor.
Breathe regularly.

introduce:
Stand with your feet a little wider than shoulder-width apart. Raise your arms at your sides to shoulder height with your palms down. 

Turn your right foot to the right and your left foot 45 degrees to the right. Slightly shift your hips to the left, and bend your torso to the right until your right hand is pressed on the floor. 

Extend your left arm toward the ceiling, and turn your head to look at your left hand. Breathe slowly and deeply. Hold this position.
name: TRIANGLE POSE RIGHT

tips.text: Please keep your chest facing forward.
Please keep your arms and legs straight during the exercise.
If you feel it\'s too hard, put your right hand on your right leg instead of the floor.
Breathe regularly.

introduce: Lie on your back with your legs stretched, hands at your sides and palms up. Take deep relaxation on the floor.\n\nTake deep breaths through your nose. Connect your body to the breath.
name: RELAXATION LYING POSE

tips.text: Close your eyes, relax your arms and legs, relax your face, relax the ankles.
Take deep breaths through your nose.
Let any weight, any tension relax to the earth, feel the floor below you, supporting you.
Let every part of your body relax and lower to the ground.
Invite rest and peace into your mind, body and soul.

introduce:
Stand with feet a little wider than shoulder width apart. 

Raise your hands overhead with palms up toward the ceiling. 

Use one of your hands to grab the other. Bend your body side to side.
name: STANDING BACK STRETCHES

tips.text: Inhale when you bend down, and exhale when you come back.
This exercise helps stretch your spine.

introduce:
Stand straight with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart. Lift your arms to the sides at shoulder height, and bend your knees slightly. 

Then push your hips back, bend your body and touch the left toe with your right hand. Return to the starting position. 

Switch sides and repeat the exercise.
name: STANDING CROSSOVER TOE TOUCHES

tips.text: Keep your back straight the whole time.
Exhale when you bend your body down, and inhale when you get up.
If it is too hard for you, bend in your knees more when you reach for your toes.
You should feel your oblique muscles burning.
This exercise helps tone your obliques and improve core strength.

introduce: Lie on your stomach with your legs extended and your arms by your sides. \n\nLift your shoulders, legs, and arms off the floor with your palms toward the ceiling. Breathe normally. Hold this position.
name: LOCUST POSE

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Keep your pelvis on the floor when lifting your legs.
Breathe naturally.
This exercise tones your buttocks and strengthens your back muscles.

introduce:
Start in a lunge position, but with your right leg on the floor. Tuck your pelvis in and sink your hips. 

Raise your arms up by your ears with your palms facing each other. Look straight ahead. Hold this position.

Take full and deep breaths. Lengthen your spine each time you exhale.
name: CRESCENT LOW LUNGE LEFT

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Keep your front knee facing forward.
Don\'t let your front knee go over your toes.
This exercise stretches your hips, chest, and belly.
This exercise strengthens your thighs and shoulders.
Breathe regularly.

introduce:
Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart. Turn your left foot to the left and your right foot 60 degrees to the left.

Lower your body until your left thigh is almost parallel to the floor. Raise your arms to your sides with your palms down.

Draw your belly in, tuck your tailbone down, and lift your chest. Take your gaze to your left hand. 

Breathe in deeply and breathe out completely. Hold this position.
name: WARRIOR Ⅱ LEFT

tips.text: Keep your bent knee in line with your toes.
Keep your torso in the middle.
Draw your shoulders away from your ears and keep them relaxed.
Don\'t let your bent knee go over your toes.
Keep your feet flat on the floor.
This exercise strengthens your thighs, shoulders, and back.
This exercise stretches your chest, hips, and hamstrings.
Breathe regularly.

introduce:
Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart. Turn your right foot to the right and your left foot 60 degrees to the right.

Lower your body until your right thigh is almost parallel to the floor. Raise your arms to your sides with your palms down.

Draw your belly in, tuck your tailbone down, and lift your chest. Take your gaze to your right hand. 

Breathe in deeply and breathe out completely. Hold this position.
name: WARRIOR Ⅱ RIGHT

tips.text: Keep your bent knee in line with your toes.
Keep your torso in the middle.
Draw your shoulders away from your ears and keep them relaxed.
Don't let your bent knee go over your toes.
Keep your feet flat on the floor.
This exercise strengthens your thighs, shoulders, and back.
This exercise stretches your chest, hips, and hamstrings.
Breathe regularly.

introduce:
Start in a lunge position, but with your left leg on the floor. Tuck your pelvis in and sink your hips. 

Raise your arms up by your ears with your palms facing each other. Look straight ahead. Hold this position.

Take full and deep breaths. Lengthen your spine each time you exhale.
name: CRESCENT LOW LUNGE RIGHT

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Keep your front knee facing forward.
Don't let your front knee go over your toes.
This exercise stretches your hips, chest, and belly.
This exercise strengthens your thighs and shoulders.
Breathe regularly.

introduce:
Lie down on your stomach and bend your elbows with your hands beneath your shoulders.

Keep your toes back and your feet and legs relaxed on the ground.

Exhale, push your chest up off the ground as far as possible. As you inhale, return to the start position and repeat.
name: COBRAS

tips.text: Prepare a mat first.
Tighten your abdominals.
Stretch your abdominals as much as you can.
Inhale when you go up, and exhale when you go down.
This is a great exercise to strengthen your back.
